normalized.description: Over the past decade, our understanding of Earth's core dynamics has significantly advanced, largely due to the continuous geomagnetic field data provided by the ESA Swarm mission. These long-term observations, combined with progress in geodynamo numerical modelling, have greatly improved our ability to analyse rapid magnetic field variations. However, several key questions remain unanswered, particularly regarding the causes of the eastward flow growth beneath the Pacific, the acceleration and deceleration of high-latitude jets, and some detected wave motions at specific latitudes. Further investigation is needed to understand transient core motions and the role of hydro-magnetic waves, with a strong focus on uncertainty estimation. Addressing these challenges requires extending the analysed time period to improve predictive capabilities and exploring the feasibility of machine learning methods for potential geomagnetic field forecasting. The 4D Core+ initiative is dedicated to tackling these issues, with the ultimate goal of deepening our comprehension of Earth's deep interior.
